text: A representation of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is the same thing as:
explanation: By the universal property of $\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g})$, $\mathfrak{g}$-representations correspond exactly to left $\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g})$-modules, so all of module theory applies. Ideals and subalgebras are internal structural objects, and a central element merely acts as a scalar on each irreducible — none of these is a representation.
